correctness.rationale: The distributional derivative representation of arbitrary BV inputs reduces the norm to the largest single-jump response. Direct differentiation gives (C_3 f_c)prime=(2 sqrt(1-c^2)/pi)Q_c, Q_c=(16c^2-4)x^2+4cx+2-4c^2. The two internal roots for c>=2/3 give explicit H(c)=(4/3)sqrt(1-u)[1+2u+(16u^2-11u+2)^(3/2)/(4u-1)^2]. Differentiation, exact squaring and a Sturm chain isolate exactly one stationary point on (4/9,1) at u*=.692..., with sign changing + to -. On c<=2/3 the finite exact integer/rational midpoint upper certificate M=128, grid c=k/12000 k<=8000, integral error <=24/M^2, |Hprime|<80 and grid allowance 40/12000 show max upper 2.4425881184680684 <49/20. Independent reimplementation of all 8001 integer midpoint enclosures reproduced this strict gap; at c=5/6 the exact radical witness exceeds 49/20. Since 2H/pi is norm, global maximizers ±sqrt(u*) are off-center. The exact discrete certificate plus analytic continuum bound, not finite sampling alone, closes the proof.
